utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. We adjourned last night at the point considering an interesting question. Some written submissions have been received from the Office of the Prosecutor. And there has been a suggestion that you might have some different position, Mr. Khan.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I did inform the Prosecution early this morning that in fact I was not maintaining the objection. I don't think there's going to be a dispute between the parties, in fact, as to where the Prosecution is going in relation to what he said in the statement on that issue. And so, I withdraw the objection and I have no objection for the statement to be put to the witness in a bid to refresh his memory. Accordingly, Your Honour, I don't think there needs to be any more argument on that issue, if that's where --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Chamber is grateful, Mr. Khan. I think it would be helpful if we said a word or two to guide the conduct of the trial as it progresses, as this issue may not have passed altogether from us. I know when we closed yesterday as I was handed a copy of Hadzihasanovic at the end, as I glanced through it I missed the significance of the second half of one sentence. I saw a reference to Simic, which was cross-examination, but of course the Appeals Chamber in that decision, which was last year, expressly appears to have held that the position during evidence in chief should be the same as that in- cross-examination. That being the position, although any of this is perhaps still subject to discretion, there being no unusual or particular circumstances relevant to the matter of discretion, the normal course that counsel may expect this Chamber to follow -- whether there be a similar situation whether in the course of the Prosecution case or the case of any one of the accused, it can be expected that this Chamber will follow the position indicated by the Appeals Chamber in that decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm most grateful for that, and I'm sure it provides huge assistance to the parties. I didn't want to get embroiled in what the Appeals Chamber decision says. It is perhaps not the most detailed of decisions from the Appeals Chamber. It's difficult to discern any attempt to distil a general principle of law after seeing a comparative analysis of different common-law systems. It is a decision of the Appeals Chamber, and until such time it is revisited or refined, it is not worth seeking to relitigate it. Your Honour, there may be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I would only observe there, Mr. Khan, that you may have limited the field a little, if you look at the composition of the Chamber, in your use of the word "common law."

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It is I think a further indication that the wiser influences of the civil law are taking an increasing role in the procedure of this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, and of course it hasn't escaped our attention and my attention that of course we are fortunate in having one of the pre-eminent experts in comparative criminal procedure that is adjudicating on this case. But, Your Honour, the point may be reached in which, notwithstanding the rather bare-bones approach of the Appeals Chamber, Your Honours may think it appropriate to give some guidance as to the modalities. But, Your Honour, perhaps that's for another occasion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I don't think we will spend more time on it now. You only need to see, for instance, where the sands have shifted statutorily in your country in the last two years, with the Criminal Procedure Act of 2003, which I read for the first time overnight. That, too, was quite a move. So --

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Yes, in which direction, of course --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Wherever we go it's heading in the direction of letting the court see in what the judges in -- particularly in Belgium and other civil law countries would automatically see, and in which prior statements would almost automatically be put to a witness if there was a different or an inability to remember some aspect of the evidence. But I think enough; we're --

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Indeed. I am most grateful to Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- you might expect to find the Chamber on this matter if it should arise again. That is not to try to say that you might not try to move us if you think that's necessary. But I think an indication of our present position is worthwhile in view of what was said yesterday. That being so, we might now move to have the witness back and continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: I'm most grateful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Karpuzi. If --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Honourable Gentlemen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If we could remind you of the affirmation you took at the beginning of your evidence that still applies. Mr. Nicholls has some further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Nicholls: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Karpuzi.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I now ask if we can provide the witness with a copy of his statement in the Albanian language, which we have available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you have a copy of your statement to the ICTY from July 2003 in front of you in your language?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to direct your attention to paragraph 11 of the statement. Please read that paragraph. And the section of the paragraph I'm interested in - it's a long paragraph - is about the oath ceremony that we were talking about yesterday. If you look about two-thirds of the way down you'll see the following: "The things that he spoke about made us respect him as a leader and we wanted him to be in charge. Celiku said that if we respect what he said in his speech, he would be prepared to be our leader." So please read that and find the words in your statement.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you read all of paragraph 11?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not all of it, but the part that you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please read the whole paragraph, focusing on that section.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: For the Court's edification it is a rather long paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: But in fairness, Your Honour, it concerns the whole topic, so I think he should read the whole paragraph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you finished, sir?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You can put the statement away now. Now don't need to have that in front of you anymore. I'll ask you the same question I asked you at the end yesterday. And just to be very clear, between the date of the oath ceremony and the 26th of July, did Celiku ever agree to be a leader? Now --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, excuse me, I would object to that question being asked at this time. As I understand it, the document was shown to the witness for the purpose of determining whether or not his memory was refreshed with regard to a previous statement made. If that is what is occurring, the appropriate thing at this point would be to ask the witness whether or not at this time, having reviewed that language, his memory is refreshed with regard to what was said.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That's what the rest of my statement would have been after posing the question, if his memory had been refreshed for the purpose it was asked to refresh and regarding that question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I'll ask you now, sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I am not clear what your present form of question will be. Perhaps it could be put again and we'll see whether it --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I was going to start over, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I've just read out the question from yesterday. On that topic, has reviewing your statement helped you to remember what was said and what happened at the oath ceremony?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same as yesterday. It's the same words that are in the text there in paragraph 11. And I gave the same answers yesterday, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, there may be some confusion here, which I will try to clear up. The text in paragraph 11 which you have just read states that Celiku stated that he was prepared to be the leader of the soldiers. That's what it says in your statement. In your answers to questions yesterday you stated several times that he refused to be a leader of the soldiers at the oath ceremony. So I'm confused --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me. As a matter of fact, once again Mr. Nicholls is being incomplete with regard to what the translation of the Albanian says. The translation says "Celiku said that if we respect what he said in his speech, he would be prepared to be our leader." And I think that by virtue of some of the previous answers of this particular witness, the entirety of that sentence is critical to a proper understanding of what the witness not only remembers but is testifying to in these proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That appears to be the core of this point of the question, Mr. Nicholls. Perhaps you might have the witness focus on that passage, if I understand your intention correctly, and then ask specifically about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, the sentence in paragraph 11: "Celiku said that if we respect what he said in his speech, he would be prepared to be our leader." That's what it says in your statement and you've said that your statement from 2003 was the same as your testimony yesterday. Yesterday I asked you a question: At any point during the oath ceremony did Celiku state that he would be prepared to be a leader, that he would accept to be a leader, and you stated no. That's at page 56, lines 20 to 23. Could you explain what you mean when you say that these statements are the same, are consistent.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Honourable Judges, can I explain something here? Is it possible?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yesterday I said that we asked him on the basis of the words that he had said, that the people of Kosovo is everybody, so in spite of their religion or nationality, everybody is considered the people of Kosovo. And after these words that he mentioned -- it was a very short time that he said these things, a minute or two. When he said these words, people were laughing. There were some soldiers that laughed, and he said, If you don't respect what I'm saying then I won't be your leader. So I'm saying today what I already said yesterday: that he did not accept to become a leader after the soldiers started to laugh. That was my answer yesterday; this is my answer today, the same one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever given that account to anybody else? Have you ever told anybody that before, that Celiku refused?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the statement it says that he did not accept to become our leader.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, can you point to me where it says that in your statement, if you're talking about your statement from 2003. Take your time.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here where it says what he talked about made us respect him as a leader and we wanted him to be a leader. And Celiku said that if we respected what he said in this speech, then he would be ready to become our leader. But we laughed -- I did not laugh myself but there were some people who laughed. And he went away and he said, I won't accept. He did not accept what we offered him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And -- sorry, just so I'm clear, that's your explanation as to how the statement, the part you read out which says: "The things he spoke about made us respect him as a leader and we wanted him to be in charge. Celiku said if we respect what he said in his speech, he would be prepared to be our leader" --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: He doesn't say that --

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: He says then. Then is the qualifying word with regard to the issue that is being presented here. And once again it's here, since we're not only dealing with interpretation but translation, it's critical that each and every word is put to the witness and words are not left out for purposes of making an argument within a question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The English version of the statement reads: "Celiku said that if we respect what he said in his speech, he would be prepared to be our leader." Now, there may be a "then" in the Albanian version; however, the original, the authoritative is the English. This is what was taken and what was read back. Now, I don't think it makes any difference. I'll rephrase my question with the word "then," if the witness prefers. But the English which is what was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Perhaps you might explore whether the Albanian version he has in front of him contains the word which is the subject of the submission by Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, will you please read verbatim the sentence in paragraph 11 which begins: "Celiku said that if we respect what he said in his speech". Read that sentence word for word as it appears in your language.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Aloud, you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Celiku said that if we respect the things that he spoke about in his speech, then he -- so then, he would be prepared to be our leader. So then he" --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. In any event his -- what Celiku said was that he would be prepared to be the leader, qualified on his -- what he said in his speech being accepted. Are you claiming -- and just so I understand that this sentence explains why you said yesterday that Celiku refused to be --

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I do apologise and perhaps there's no utility in my standing, but this is still examination-in-chief; it's not cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Khan. But we've got to get to the bottom of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I won't attempt to frame the question for you, Mr. Nicholls. It's clear the point you are seeking to make. The Chamber is in the difficulty that it doesn't have the statement. One thing that occurs to me is whether there is an express statement one way or the other whether leadership was accepted or not in the statement. If there is no express statement, the position for you may be more difficult.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: There is no express statement; however, the statement taken as a whole, if the Chamber would read it, would show that the witness indicates that after the oath ceremony Celiku is referred to as Commander Celiku and before the oath ceremony he is not. He is referred to simply as Celiku. There is no express --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, you haven't yet explored whether the witness's recollection of those matters remains today as it was yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, what I'm trying to explore, Your Honour, is that a little while ago the witness stated when I asked him: Have you ever told this to anybody before that Celiku refused to be a leader because his speech was not well-received and the soldiers, in the witness's words, retorted to his speech. I asked him if he ever told that to anybody before, and he said yes in his statement and then he pointed us to this passage. So what I'm simply trying to do is to have the witness clarify that answer. And to do that, I'm trying to get him to explain to us how these two statements are the same. And I don't think I've gotten there yet. What I'm trying to do is have him read the statement and in his own words explain how what he said in the statement that he meant -- that where Celiku accepted that he would be in charge, that it actually means the opposite of what he said yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It's to that point that my observations were directed. If there is no express statement of the outcome, your foundation for there being a material difference is not very secure.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, I think there is a material difference, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That's a matter for submission later, if it should ever become relevant. We're at the point of questioning now and you went on to suggest, well, the clear implication of the statement is that from that point on, for instance, Celiku was referred to as commander. Now, that is not presently the evidence. Now, if you want to see whether the evidence is affected by being refreshed by this statement in that respect, it may be something worth pursuing for you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Karpuzi, yesterday you stated that in the time period -- well, I won't summarise. I'll look at the exact quote. Yesterday I asked you on page 54: "After the oath ceremony before the 26th of July, 1998, during that period of time did you ever hear of Celiku referred to as Commander Celiku?"

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I might interject.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: We're trying to figure out a way to make this perhaps a bit easier for all. And we've just canvassed between the Defence and it might be of some assistance for the Chamber to have the statement, or at least this particular paragraph, so that you are not in the dark as we are thrashing about in an attempt to deal with evidentiary concerns. And that way the Trial Chamber may be able to focus in a way that the advocates are. Or maybe not, but who knows; but in any event, you have the information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: There was a silence about you at that point. Would you think that a practical course?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I do, Your Honour, I have no objection. But I think it needs to be the whole statement for it to have any real utility.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That would be fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- propose at this moment to read the whole statement, but paragraph 11 seems to be the point of focus.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes. And we actually have that ready. We can distribute it. I don't think it has been yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Unfortunately the last line of the page is hinted at but not present.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, that's unfortunate because that's an important line. That's unfortunate. I can read out the bottom of page 5, if that helps, and then we'll get a new cleaner copy. The last sentence on page 5 is: "He was talking about the people of Kosovo being one, regardless of ethnicity, religion, gender or such." And we can put that on Sanction I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls, there seems to be no direct reference to commander in that context. What is perhaps not here is any reference to there being some group of soldiers laughing at his words.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. The plain meaning is exactly the opposite, I would suggest. And what is also not there is any express statement by Celiku that he would not be their leader, which is what the witness stated yesterday -- the witness used the word "refused to be our leader."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Right. Now, coming back to a point made by Mr. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Guy-Smith, we are cross-examining. You are in the point at the moment of examination of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is a statement made by him you have sought and been allowed to have the witness read it to see if it refreshes his recollection. On what basis do you suggest that you can now cross-examine him about the differences, if there are any?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I don't think I'm cross-examining him, Your Honour, just asking him to clarify his answer, because to me his answer doesn't make sense where he states that this paragraph is exactly where he said what he said yesterday. So that is just what I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, you can explore that by proper questions of examination, indeed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, the same question, the same topic. I asked you about this passage in your statement, whether you had told this to anybody else. And you directed us to this portion of paragraph 11. Now, where in your statement does it say that Celiku refused to be a commander?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the interview we had problems in the beginning with investigator about such words, and I was not asked such a question, whether he was made commander or not. And I did not answer that, so I did not emphasise such a thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. That wasn't the question, whether you were asked whether he was a commander or not. My question was about where in here you say he refused, because what you've told us and what I understood you to say was that this is what you meant by this sentence, that Celiku refused to be commander.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This question was not asked, and that's why I did not give an answer about it, whether he was made or not a commander. If they had asked me the question, I would have answered it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where in that paragraph or in the statement --

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, it goes back to the beginning of this session. My learned friend put the document as a memory-refreshing document; that was the ambit of the statement. The witness has looked at the statement and has been asked if it refreshes his memory. Your Honour, I think it's quite clear what my submission is; my friend should put questions of the proper form. I don't think there's any real dispute between the parties as to what the witness said; the witness's evidence is clear. If my friend asked proper questions to the point, I don't think we will be in any difficulty. Your Honour, that's my observation at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Khan. There may be, Mr. Nicholls, if I may venture a suggestion, other points where you feel the evidence of the witness is at some variance to what is here. If you want to explore the witness's present recollection about those matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I will, Your Honour, but just to say why I think this line I've been following is proper is the witness's response to the question: Have you ever told anybody about this before that Celiku refused? Yes. And he pointed to this paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: He pointed to it. Now you want to say it is different; but you haven't by questions that are questions in-chief sought to expose those differences.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you remember in your statement talking about when Celiku became referred to as a commander? Do you remember talking about that topic?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was it that you first started hearing about Celiku --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I hate to interject, but the common practice when dealing with refreshing a witness's memory is to point counsel to the part of the statement that you're referring so we can follow along with you, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: We can jump ahead and go to paragraph 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, Witness, could you read paragraph 6, please, in your statement, and let me know when you're done.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I read it, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. Nicholls, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that help you remember these events at all?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are already in my memory. Even without reading them I remember the things that have happened. And the things that I remembered, I expressed them here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Good. Now, did you ever hear - I'll go back to yesterday - Celiku referred to as Commander Celiku?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember whether you ever heard Celiku referred to as Commander Celiku?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is also in the statement that by October and November we heard that he became a commander. This is what I said in the statement, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I refer you to yesterday, page 53, line 18, when the witness gave the same answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Khan, but I don't think you need to remind us of those matters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the question was - let me ask you again: When was the first time, just to be clear, that you heard Celiku referred to as Commander Celiku?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: October or November.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when was the first time that you heard of Celiku, of this person called Celiku?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As Celiku, I heard this name, Celik, I heard this name after the oath ceremony. But as Commander Celiku I heard that name, Commander Celiku, in October or November 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Excuse me one moment, Witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you, Witness - again this is a question from yesterday - Do you know what Haradin Bala's pseudonym was in May of 1998?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Shala.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And is that the name you knew him by in May 1998?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And let me try to ask you another question. You've said that it was after the oath ceremony that you first heard about Celiku, and you said yesterday you saw him two or three times between the oath ceremony and the 26th of July battle. What were you doing on those times when you saw Celiku? What were the circumstances of those meetings?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean what I was doing or what Celiku was doing?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What both of you were doing.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We met on -- in the course of fighting on the defence line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what were you actually during that fighting -- I'm sorry. Can you tell me specifically as best you remember what were you doing during that fighting, what type of weapon you were using, anything you can remember.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, what period are you asking me about? If you can explain that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am talking about the period -- well, you stated you had never met Celiku before the oath ceremony. So I'm talking about the period between the oath ceremony, which you stated yesterday was between the end of June/early July, and the 26th of July when you were wounded in battle. That's the period.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mentioned it earlier, that during that period I saw him two or three times, including the ceremony during that period in the course of fighting, in defence line. As all the other comrades, we had a very strong enemy in front of us so we were fighting, all of us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question is: If you remember, how were you fighting? What were you doing during those times that you were at the front line or fighting with Celiku?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were fighting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was Celiku doing?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same, he was fighting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where was he staying at that time, if you know? And I'm speaking specifically about where he was staying at the times you met him between the oath ceremony and 26th of July.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know where he stayed. I know only about that day when we were fighting that we received some port [as interpreted] from many people and we were fighting, all of us. The Serbian forces were in front of us. I don't know where he was during the fighting. I would say that he was in a position where he could shoot, where he could kill paramilitaries or soldiers. And, you know, even if my brother had been there next to me, I wouldn't be able to tell you now what exactly my brother was doing there next to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we could send the witness out for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Karpuzi, would you be kind enough to wait outside the court for a little while. There must be a matter which counsel debates with the Chamber. So if you could wait outside a little while, we'll call you in as soon as we've dealt with that matter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would only be happy to do that, Honourable Judges.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Can we go into private session for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I take it, Your Honour, the next break will be approximately 6.00 p.m. or is it ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I would target a little before 6.00 I think, Mr. Nicholls, 10 to, 5 to, depending on how the evidence is at that moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm sorry you had such a long wait outside, but we've managed to deal with the matters that were raised and Mr. Nicholls will continue with his questioning now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you hear me all right, Mr. Karpuzi?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember what the first thing you said into that microphone was when you came into court yesterday?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I took the oath to say the truth and only the truth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's right. And one of the first questions I asked you was about your statement made to the ICTY on the 19th and 21st of July, 2003. I asked: "Were you truthful to the best of your belief and memory when you made that statement?" And you stated that you were. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I also asked you about the signed statement which you made here in The Hague on Sunday where you made corrections to your 2003 statement, and you testified that you were truthful in that statement as well. Right?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I want to talk a little bit just for a moment about your interview in 2003. That took place in your home. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Over two days?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Lehtinen asked you questions and you gave him answers?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if you allow me, I would like to make an explanation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When Mr. Lehtinen questioned me -- I mean, when he came for the first time, he asked me these words. He addressed me saying that, You are Mr. Ruzhdi Karpuzi? And I said, Yes. And you have your pseudonym Shala? Yes. You have been a member in the Lapusnik battle? Yes, I said. Then he said, On the authority of Mrs. Carla Del Ponte we are here to take a statement by you. Having respect for the Tribunal and for the General Prosecutor, I accepted to make the statement which you might have seen by now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Karpuzi. And while you spoke and answered questions and made statements, Mr. Lehtinen typed up what you said on a laptop. Right? He made notes?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After taking the statement was done, it was printed and read back to you by an interpreter. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. During -- when they read me the statement, I had many reserves, but since I'm not a well-educated person I may have understood them differently from you, since as I said I don't have many years of schooling.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after the statement was read back to you in your home, you were given the chance to make any changes to it, to fix any mistakes?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Indeed, it was -- when it came to the signing of the statement, I had to tell the interpreter, Sir, are you interpreting -- are you telling him what I'm saying or the guy who is taking notes, he is writing what he wants? If he's writing what he likes, then I'm not going to sign this statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But after the statement was read back to you, you did sign it.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you signed it - I can show it to you if you like - under a block of text which states that the statement was true to the best of your knowledge and recollection.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you and I met one day in your house last October. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the month, but yes I remember that you were there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just briefly. And then the next time we met was Sunday morning here in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were given a copy of your statement in the Albanian language, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because you wanted to read it, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were given a green felt-tip pen so you could make any notes while you were reading of things you thought were important.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not about the things that were important, but as I said, even earlier I had some reserves, some contestations. That's why things which might have happened during the interpretation or when he was taking down notes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Which is why we had you read your entire statement in the Albanian language and you were told you could fix any mistakes. Right?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, that calls for speculation on the witness's part as to why they had him read his statement unless that was explained to him at the time the statement was just given.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That's what I just said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It's nearly what you said, but you might just make it a little clearer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were given a copy of your 2003 statement in the Albanian language. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were given a felt-tip pen. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were told you could take your time, as long as you needed, to read the statement. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were told to make notes on the statement if there was anything you wanted to correct.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was given the felt-tip pen to make my corrections where I felt I should, and this is what I did as far as I was able to understand. The things that were most striking in the statement I corrected.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. And you spent about 40 minutes reviewing your statement and making some notes. Right?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I can't tell you how long it took me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you remember you worked for a while and then we had a break to have a cigarette and a cup of tea and then you went back and finished reading your statement. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you did make some notations on the Albanian copy of your statement with a green pen, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Sorry. One second, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to give you a copy of your witness statement of Sunday, the 6th of February being made here in The Hague and we'll just go through it a little bit. Now, you don't need to read it right now, but just like your first statement in 2003, after this statement was taken it was read back to you in Albanian by an interpreter. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again, at the end you signed that this statement was true to the best of your ability to remember, recollect, and speak the truth?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When do you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I mean on Sunday when you signed your statement making corrections.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You signed that "it contains everything I said to the best of my knowledge and recollection," that's specifically what it says.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's how it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please take a look at that statement which should be before you in Albanian. Do you have a copy? I'm just asking you now if you have a copy, sorry.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And let's look at paragraph 2. It states: "Today on 6th February 2005, I have met with investigator Ole Lehtinen and attorney Julian Nicholls at the ICTY in The Hague to prepare for my testimony in court." Do you see that sentence?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "An Albanian translation of my previous statement was given to me to read and I reviewed it carefully." Do you see that sentence?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's how it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "After reviewing the statement, I have made the following corrections to the representatives of the Office of the Prosecutor." That's what it states. Right?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's in fact exactly what happened on Sunday, isn't it? You read your statement carefully and then you made some corrections to it.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, in paragraph 3 of your statement of Sunday you made a correction to paragraph 6 of your 2003 statement. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what you wanted to do there was correct in paragraph 6 the way it was written in paragraph 6, that some of the villagers had no actual weapons when you had stated that some of them did have axes and other weapons. You wanted to clarify that part of paragraph 6. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The -- in the first statement I -- it was written that they came there with some axes, but when I made the statement maybe it was my mistake or the interpreter's mistake because I did not specify properly. So in your presence, Mr. Nicholls, I said that the villagers came not without weapons but with weapons, some carrying weapons, some carrying axes, some carrying forks, and so on. This was my correction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, in paragraph 4, speaking of the statement you gave on Sunday, you found a mistake in paragraph 7 of your 2003 statement. And do you have copies of both statements in front of you, Mr. Karpuzi? Do you have two statements there?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you can refer to both of them if you need to. And you found a mistake in paragraph 7 of the Albanian translation that you had been given to read. In the Albanian version in paragraph 7 it stated that you did know of the headquarters above Lapusnik. And you wanted to make it clear that what you had stated was that you did not know of any command above Lapusnik. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was how it was written, but in my conversation with Ole and the interpreter, in English it was written what I said and my remark after I corrected it. But in Albanian, it was that "I have known." In English, it was "I have not known."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. So Mr. Lehtinen made it clear to you that the English statement was correct, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And we --

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: For that part we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And in your supplemental statement, though, you noted that you had found this mistake in the Albanian language. Right?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next correction you found was in paragraph 8 -- of the 2003 statement, to be clear. You wanted to clarify that what you meant by -- that Gzim Gashi's house, calling it a main point, was not that it was a main point for the KLA in Lapusnik but it was a main point for you and other soldiers. Right?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was recorded in your statement on Sunday as well?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In paragraph 14 of the 2003 statement, you found another point where you needed to make a correction. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You stated -- you state in the statement of last Sunday that you want to be clear that you were in such a bad state after being injured on 26th July 1998 that you have no clear recollection of how you in fact arrived in Klecka. That was the correction you needed to make. Right?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls, if you allow me, when you were present in the presence of Lehtinen and the interpreter - I apologise for not knowing her name - when you visited me at my home, even then I made this objection. But Lehtinen told me, When you come there you can explain whether that was so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. And then when you came here you did fix that part of your statement about the bad state you were in when you were taken to Klecka after being wounded.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next correction you made was in paragraph 15 of your 2003 statement. That mention -- that paragraph described you as saying that you were a squad leader after returning to your own village.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You corrected the statement to describe your position as a leader of a group of friends in the village?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those were all the corrections you had to make to your 2003 statement?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, to my recollection, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, if you look at your next paragraph, 8, you state: "Other than these corrections made in this statement, the statement taken in July 2003 is accurate." Right?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I want to ask you a couple of questions about your 2003 statement. Let me take you first to paragraph 11. Could you look at paragraph 11, please. Do you have that in front of you, sir?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, that statement starts off, and I'll paraphrase, that one day in June or July 1998 Voglushi gathered all the soldiers together in the yard of the house that was next to the compound that's been mentioned as a prison. And that's correct, isn't it? The soldiers did all --

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There was a house and a flagpole in that yard. That's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you told us yesterday - and we saw the diagram that you had marked - that that was a house of Bali Vojvoda. That's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the statement says that: "Three persons raised the flag."

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were one of the persons who participated in the flag-raising ceremony. That's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that, there was a short oath read and the soldiers repeated it. Right?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you don't remember exactly what the text was. That's what you said yesterday, that's what it says in the statement, and that's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you read all through this paragraph when you were reviewing your statement on Sunday.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, after the oath was taken there was a gathering where Celiku gave a short speech. That's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Can I give an explanation if possible?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You may.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not a meeting. After the oath was concluded, when we broke up, we -- the group of friends, this is when these words were uttered. It lasted one or two minutes. I told this even to Ole.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Look at the sentence in your copy in Albanian which states: "After the oath was taken, there was a gathering where Celiku gave a short speech." Does the word, and I may pronounce it wrong, "fjalim," appear in that sentence?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is the word "a gathering."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm talking about the word for speech.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the statement it's called a speech.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's a short speech.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Celiku gave a short speech. That's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you don't remember all the details of that speech, understandably, but you recall that Celiku talked about the importance of protecting and being careful with the civilians. That's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He talked about the people of Kosovo people being one regardless of ethnicity, religion, or gender. You remember that being said?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "The things that he spoke about made us respect him as a leader and we wanted him to be in charge," and I've had the Albanian checked. The Albanian translation says, "and we wanted him to be our leader." That's what it says in the statement you've got. Right?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Celiku said that if we respect what he said in his speech he would be prepared to be our leader. That's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: True.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's exactly what happened at the oath ceremony, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I want you to look at paragraph 12, please. And maybe we can clear this up. I want to help me understand. This is another paragraph that -- this is a paragraph that you didn't have to make any corrections to. Now, the first sentence is that the oath ceremony was the first time you saw Celiku. That's correct, isn't it? That was the first time you saw him in person? Is that what you remember?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, to my recollection.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't see him on the 8th or 9th of May, 1998, during the fighting?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then it states: "The investigator asked me on how many occasions I saw Celiku in Lapusnik and I think it was approximately three." And that's right, isn't it? You saw Celiku in Lapusnik about three times?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you remember I asked you yesterday about that time period how -- whether -- I asked you yesterday about the time period between the oath ceremony and July 26th when you were injured fighting. And you stated that it was during that period of time that you saw Celiku about three times in Lapusnik. Right?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And next you say in your sentence -- in your statement: "He might have visited there more often, but this is what I know." And that's true, isn't it? You stated what you knew.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said what I knew.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What you knew was that he'd been there about three times, but that it could have been more; however you didn't see him on those other occasions.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And you remember him coming to greet you and the other soldiers in fighting positions "to see how the trench-digging was proceeding and such." That's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, to see how the trenches were being dug. I don't remember to have said this, but it's true that I have saw him during the fighting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me be very clear. You saw him during the fighting between the oath ceremony and July 26th in Lapusnik. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also saw him in Lapusnik between the end of -- between the oath ceremony and the 26th of July when he came to see how the trench-digging was proceeding?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not how the trench-digging was proceeding, because at a period the trenches were already dug. But during the fighting I've seen him in the trenches fighting along with us, because as I said people were coming to our rescue from various villages. We didn't know who they were and it was not our right to ask them. We didn't have the time to see where they were coming from or who they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The question I asked you just a moment ago was: You remember him, Celiku, coming to greet you and the other soldiers in fighting positions to see how the trench-digging was proceeding and such? And you stated: "Yes, to see how the trenches were being dug." Right? That's what you answered just a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Look at the statement in front of you. All right. "I remember him coming to greet us in the fighting positions to see how the trench-digging was proceeding and such." Do you see that sentence?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see this sentence. I see it, but I'm here to tell the truth and it's more than true that I've seen him in the front line during the fighting. I said even earlier that maybe I'm incapable of having the same understanding of things, of sentences, as you. I cannot go into depth like you might, and some things might have happened. He might have written this, but I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. "I remember him coming to greet us in the fighting positions to see how the trench-digging was proceeding and such." Is there anything about that sentence that you don't understand when you read it?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There isn't anything that I understand as far as the sentence goes, but I don't remember that I have said this, that he came to visit us to -- in the front line, in the fighting line. He fought with us in this defence line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the next sentence is: "I cannot remember ever seeing him at Gzim's compound." That's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you were reviewing your statement, you had your pen and you carefully reviewed your statement, you didn't make any marks here, did you?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not clear. What do you mean? Where?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I mean is you've just told me, and I know you're right, that there's nothing confusing at all about that sentence which states that Celiku visited to see how proceedings were going during the trench-digging. When you reviewed your statement on Sunday, when you had time to make notes on the statement, when you had time to correct your statement, you didn't say anything about that sentence, did you?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's true that I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's because you know that it's true.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm repeating that the truth is that I've seen him in the defence line during the fighting. You may write what you like, you may interpret it the way you want; I'm saying this, what I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But we didn't write what we liked, we wrote -- Mr. Lehtinen wrote what you said and that's why you were allowed to check the statement to make sure that it was accurate --

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, again it may be pointless to rise to object, but again, there is a distinction between arguing with a witness and cross-examining a witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You're on the edge, Mr. Nicholls. It would be safer to move back.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'll move back, Your Honour. One second, Your Honour. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me go to paragraph 6 of your statement please, sir, of your 2003 statement. Now, in that statement you begun talking about how there was no actual command in Lapusnik when you first arrived there. That's correct, isn't it, in your view?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Voglushi was a respected man among the soldiers. Right?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was picked to be a leader?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was killed fighting in Lapusnik on the 26th of July, 1998, as it says in this paragraph. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's the same day that you were injured.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 18th of May - and you testified about this yesterday - there was more fighting in Lapusnik, another attempt by the Serbs to take over. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the 18th or 19th, I'm not very certain which of the two, but it must have been one of the two. That is the time I meant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on that day, whether it was the 18th or 19th as it says in your statement, you remember a man called Fehmi Lladrovci who came to Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not that I remembered at a moment, but it was Lehtinen who reminded me of this -- of this person being there in the fighting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What your statement says is that you remember a man called Fehmi Lladrovci came to Lapusnik. Right?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is as I'm saying. The investigator Ole Lehtinen asked me: Were you present during a speech given by Fehmi Lladrovci? It was at a moment that I remembered that that person was in the fighting, but I did not remember his speech. Maybe I was in the position. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I didn't ask you anything about a speech. My point is the statement is correct where it says that you remember a man called Fehmi Lladrovci came to Lapusnik at this time.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: With respect to whether I stated this and Ole asked me if it's possible, I would kindly ask him to ask me whether it was he who remembered -- recalled me -- reminded me of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not asking who reminded who. Try to just answer the question. What you stated was that Ole asked you if you had been at a meeting or heard a speech by this man, and you did not remember that speech. Right?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the speech, but I remembered after Ole reminded me that he was there together with his wife. Both of them were soldiers in the KLA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's about five or ten minutes before you said. It would be a good time for a break, if possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We'll have the second break now and barring some further interruption we'll resume at 5 minutes past 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I have a few more questions on paragraph 6 of your 2003 statement. The fighting you're talking about in that paragraph is a second attempt around the 18th or 19th of May of the Serbs to re-take Lapusnik.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A part of your statement there which we've just discussed about remembering Fehmi Lladrovci, we're talking the period around 18th and 19th of May, 1998?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were asked whether you had attended a meeting with Fehmi Lladrovci around the days of these fightings by Mr. Lehtinen, and you told him that you hadn't attended any such meeting around the 18th/19th of May, 1998. Right?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During this fighting, the 18th and 19th of May, 1998, a lot of villagers came to support you.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Some had weapons, some had axes and things like that. Right?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This also led to an increased number of soldiers in Lapusnik during the coming days. Right?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time of the oath-taking ceremony that I will describe later, I would estimate that there were some 50 to 60 soldiers. And that's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What you're talking about here in this statement is the period between the 18th and 19th of May, 1998, and the oath-taking ceremony, which is in late June or early July 1998. Right?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what you're explaining there -- since you testified yesterday in the beginning there were only a few soldiers in Lapusnik -- this number grew after the 18th and 19th of May until it was around 50 or 60 at the end of June, early July. That's the period we're talking about. Right?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were asked when you first heard talks about Commander Celiku, and you stated: "I would say it was around these same times we started hearing rumours about a General Command of the KLA and about Celiku." And that's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: With respect to a General Command, the fact is we referred to it in order to increase the morale -- to raise the morale. But actual terms, we didn't know about it. Regarding Celiku as a commander, this I learned sometime later, October or November 1998. This is what I stated even before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's look at what you stated in the statement. "I didn't say, and if I did it's a mistake, Commander Celiku, I didn't." This was the time when you first heard talks about Celiku. At this time he was not called a commander.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he was not called a commander from 18th of May, 1998, around there, until the end of June, early July. Right?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't hear people addressing him as Commander Celiku.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. During that period, I just want to be clear on this, it was only Celiku?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't hear it well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll repeat my question. During the period we're discussing, 18th of May, 1998, roundabouts 18th, 19th of May, to the end of June, early July, you did not hear Celiku referred to as Commander Celiku. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: But we were members of Celiku unit ourselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. And you -- answer the question, please. Tell me if you need me to ask it again.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I answered it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I wasn't asking you whether you were members of the Celiku unit. I'll try again. Listen carefully, please, and you can look at your statement if you want to. Between the 18th and 19th of May, 1998, until the end of June, early July, you did not hear of Celiku referred to as Commander Celiku. Right?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't hear it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time the only way you heard him referred to was as Celiku, not as any kind of commander. Right?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't seem to remember it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't seem to remember whether he was referred to as Commander Celiku or you don't seem to remember to refer -- is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember this as what you are saying.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I'll try to make it very simple. During the time period we're talking about, the time period you're talking about in paragraph 6, Celiku was only known to you as Celiku. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time I didn't know him absolutely at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I know you didn't know him. I know you hadn't met him until the oath ceremony. But what your statement says -- your statement which you've reviewed, your statement which you've sworn under oath is correct -- is that about this time you heard rumours about Celiku. And that's right, isn't it? Not that he was a commander, but you heard of Celiku?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I have stated even earlier that I didn't hear people calling him Commander Celiku until October, November. But I did hear the word "Celiku," meaning our Celiku, we who were members of Celiku unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's look at your statement. Look at your statement, please. Bottom of paragraph 6. "The investigator has asked me when I first heard talks about Commander Celiku." Do you see that sentence?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "I'd say that it was during these same times we started hearing rumours about a General Command of the KLA and about Celiku." That's what it says, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is what I said before. It's the same thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The question is: That's what it says in your statement. Right?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is what it's written here. "The investigator asked me when I first heard about Commander Celiku I would say that during that time we started to hear words about a General Command of the KLA and about Celiku." This is what it's written.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the next sentence is: "At this time he was not called Commander." Right?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were talking in that sentence about Celiku, the man, the person. Right?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: About the man, but I have said here that I didn't know who Celiku was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. You didn't know who he was. But we're not talking about a Celiku unit in these last three sentences, we're talking about Celiku the person you later learned to be Fatmir Limaj. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now: "Only after the oath ceremony I have heard this expression." That's what it says in the statement. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the first time you met Celiku was at the oath ceremony. Right?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before that time you had never heard him referred to as commander. Right? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before that time you had only heard the name Celiku of this person, although you had not met him.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean our unit?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. We're talking about the three sentences here. I know that you would have heard about the name of the unit that you were in at the time you were in the unit. That's got nothing to do with this question.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid I don't get it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I'll try to speed this along. Read the last four sentences just quietly to yourself of paragraph 6.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I may say that during that time we started hearing words about a General Command and about Celiku it is said here. At that time he was not called commander. It was only after the oath ceremony that I heard this expression. After the oath was taken, after the Lapusnik gorge fell, it was then that I heard this expression.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The question was just to ask you to read those last four sentences. Now, in those four sentences everywhere it states Celiku we're talking about -- it refers to Celiku the person. Correct? I think you've already answered that as yes.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean yes? I said here about the General Command and Celiku, our unit Celiku.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in the next sentence when you -- it states: "At this time he was not called commander." Right?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A unit as a group of men in an army is never called a commander, is it?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you say: "At this time he was not called commander," you're talking about the man Celiku?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're talking about the period between the 18th or 19th of May and the end of June or early July. Right?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The words here, "at that time he was not called a commander," meaning that when Ole asked me -- he asked me: What did Commander Celiku do at that time? I responded that in fact he was not a commander, but after the Lapusnik gorge fell he was appointed a commander. And this is when I heard about him because at the time I was not interested in many things. It was in October or November that I heard the name mentioned as Commander Celiku.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. You state at the bottom of this paragraph: "Only after the oath ceremony have I heard this expression," meaning that he was called commander. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the ceremony, oath ceremony, and after the Lapusnik gorge fell, it was in October or November, sometimes around that time, that I heard this expression.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
