utterances.text: My question is: This is what it says in your statement at the bottom of paragraph 6. Right? "At this time he was not called Commander. Only after the oath ceremony have I heard this expression." The question is: That's what it says in the statement?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you read this statement over when you reviewed -- you read this paragraph over when you reviewed your statement and you made changes to this paragraph. Right? Look at paragraph 6 of your statement of last Sunday.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I read it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you carefully reviewed this statement and you made one change. The only change you made was about the villagers and whether they had weapons. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your testimony is that after the oath ceremony, the same one we've been talking about where the soldiers asked Celiku if he would be their commander, when you say "after the oath ceremony" you're talking about September, October, November?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember talking yesterday about how it was in September, October, or November that you heard Celiku referred to as commander of the area? This is on page 53.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I asked you which area, and you said: "Brigade 121."

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I asked you which units made up Brigade 121.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said "all the small groups that were there from Kizhareke, Nekovce, Bajice, Kroimire, Pjetershtice, Carraleve, up to Luznica," all these areas merged into the 121. Right? Let's do it this way: You tell me --

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I mentioned beginning from Kizhareke. I did not mention Likovc -- Nekovce. By Shale, Pjetershtice, up to Luznica, I said. All of them merged into the 121st Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me give you a copy of map 6 from P1.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: We can give him the copy that was exhibited yesterday perhaps. We don't have another blank copy here. That's P127 for the record. Can you put that on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You remember, sir, we looked at that map yesterday and you marked on it the location of the -- of some of the units that you were familiar with, Guri, Pellumbi, Celiku.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation] --

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps my friend can deal with it. There appears to be an error on LiveNote at line 11. It appears that the witness did -- 16 on the main monitor -- that the witness did not say Nekovce but -- Your Honour, I think I should stand when it's sorted out. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Khan. Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can I just ask who is -- where this transcript correction is coming from?

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's not my habit to answer questions from counsel. I've already I think apologised to the Court for interjecting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Khan, is the source the interpreter that you have assisting you?

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, the interpreter -- to answer your question, the interpreter conveyed a message.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. Very well. There shouldn't be any fuss about that. Often there have been errors in transcript, and if they can be corrected that will be useful to everybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you talked yesterday about the 121st Brigade being formed in September, October, or November. Right?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know exactly when it was formed.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. I didn't know. I don't know exactly when that Brigade was formed because I was injured and I didn't care much what went on around me, how it happened, how it was formed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, look at the map please and tell me from this map if you can, I'll try to make it clear, which area fell within the 121st Brigade when it was formed. You started talking about the units, where they were from yesterday.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the units by name, with the exception of our unit, Celiku 3. How the other units were called, this I don't know. I can only tell you -- describe you the territory covered by this brigade, 121, that was formed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's exactly what I would like you to do, please. And can we give you a pen, please. Can you just draw a circle. I know you won't be able to do the exactly, but as best you can the area of the 121st Brigade when it was formed.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is approximately the one.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. And I won't read off all the names of the towns, but the witness has drawn a large circle extending below south of Lapusnik in an oval shape over to Malisevo and back around.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this was the area that was the area of responsibility of the 121st Brigade when it was formed?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Fatmir Limaj was the commander of the 121st Brigade when it was formed?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have information that this is how it was. I don't know exactly, but in the beginning that's what was said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let me ask you again about your answer on paragraph 6. When you were asked about when you first heard talks about Commander Celiku you stated: "Only after the oath ceremony have I heard this expression." Correct?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said after the oath, but October or November, that's when I heard this expression. It's the umpteenth time that I'm repeating this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. I'm talking about your statement that you reviewed, that you checked, that you corrected, statements only after the oath ceremony have I heard this statement Commander Celiku. That's pretty easy, yes or no. That's what the statement says.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Even earlier I explained these things to Ole and to you that later, after the oath -- later, much later, in October or November I heard this expression at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've made that explanation many times. Your testimony on that that you've tried to put forward is clear. I just want to ask this one more time and then I'll stop. Read the last sentence of paragraph 6. It states: "Only after the oath ceremony I have heard this expression." Correct? Yes or no, please.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says, but I explained when I heard it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Try to just answer the question I ask you. You've explained many times now that it was after the formation of the 121st Brigade you now say is when you first heard of Fatmir Limaj as Celiku, Commander Celiku. Right?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that's in September, October, or November 1998. Right?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately at that time. I can't remember exactly when it was when I heard it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So when you were asked in your interview when the first time was that you heard of Commander Celiku, why do you say "after the oath ceremony"? You don't say after the fall of Lapusnik, you don't say after the formation of the 121st Brigade, you don't say in September, October, or November. Why do you say "after the oath ceremony"?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat the last part of the question, please -- oh, right. I said that -- after the oath ceremony. When Ole asked me: Did you hear this at the oath ceremony? And I said: No, I didn't hear that at that time; I heard that after the formation of the 121st Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You made this statement over two days. You've sworn it was correct. You've checked it and you've stated here under oath that it's true. Right? This is the 2003 statement.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The statement says you were asked what time you heard that Celiku was a commander. Right? Let me -- sorry. Strike that. The statement says: "When the investigator asked me when I first heard talks about Commander Celiku." Right? That's what the statement says.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You read that. You didn't correct it. You didn't say: No, the investigator has asked me if I heard of Celiku being Commander Celiku at the time of the oath ceremony. That leading question does not appear in the statement, does it?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not in the statement, but the reality is that you can ask Ole about it, whether it was like that or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have linked in your mind the time that Fatmir Limaj became called Commander Celiku at the formation of the 121st Brigade. Right?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question. Could you repeat it, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You stated here several times that your recollection of when you first heard of Celiku referred to as Commander Celiku was when he became commander of the 121st Brigade. Right?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were asked the question: When did you first hear talks about Commander Celiku? Your answer is: "Only after the oath ceremony have I heard this expression." My question is why you didn't say "in September, October, November," why you didn't say "when the brigade was formed"?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know why I didn't say it, but this is the reality. And where is my answer that says that I have heard it at that period?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You read through this statement and you didn't make any corrections to this paragraph other than the part about the villagers, correct? And their weapons.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Honourable Chamber, I explained it earlier that I don't know things the way you know them, the way you emphasise them. I can't draw the essence of things that you think about. I look at the statement as it is now. I said the truth the way I knew it and I'm still saying the things I know, and that is it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you know that when the 121st Brigade was formed, Fatmir Limaj was its commander. Right?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what I heard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Did you hear what units he commanded before he was made commander of the 121st Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear of him commanding any units in August?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did not hear anything about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I mean August 1998. Did you hear of him commanding any units in July 1998?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You testified today and yesterday that he was fighting alongside you when you saw him in Lapusnik between the oath ceremony in the end of June, beginning of July.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not clear about the period; if you could say that again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're right; it's a bad question. You testified today and yesterday that the times you saw Fatmir Limaj in Lapusnik in person were between the oath ceremony and the 26th of July battle. Right?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were testifying essentially that he was fighting as an ordinary soldier, that he was no commander. Right?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You testified that he wasn't visiting the troops at the trenches to see how trench-digging and other such activities were continuing. Right?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not keep watch on him, what he was coming for there. But I don't know whether he came for that. I saw him fighting in the positions, just like all of us, all the rest of us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Now, is your testimony then that Celiku became commander of the 121st Brigade of the area you've drawn on the map and all those villages without ever commanding any other units beforehand?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you don't know which units Celiku may have commanded before he became the commander of the 121st Brigade. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you a couple questions on a different topic. You talked yesterday about how you kept records in Gzim Gashi's compound.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me when you started that record-keeping.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly, but some time -- a month and a half before the Lapusnik gorge fell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you do that full time? Was that your only job during that time, keeping records?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not only that task. I also had guard duties when we went to the positions to observe the terrain. But also when a new soldier came I had to take his details, where he was from, whether he was married or not, what kind of weapon he had, whether he had a weapon at all. This was my task.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about the if the soldier was issued a weapon? Would you keep track of that?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I know - and we'll talk about it later - that you were injured in the battle on July 26th when you were fighting. My question is: Before those injuries did you have any physical disabilities?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe what those were, speaking now about May, June 1998.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Earlier I had an accident and I was injured earlier. That is it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you describe how you were injured and what the injury was, please.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This happened -- the tractor -- I was run over by the tractor and I was injured. I broke my knee, but with the passing of time I felt better.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was that broken -- when was that injury when you broke your knee?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, not the knee. It's --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter does not understand the word "kuka."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I think you've just indicated your left thigh. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the hip.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The hip. When did you have that injury, your broken hip? When did that happen?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: There is no translation --

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The accident happened in 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I've noticed you limping when you come in and out of court. Is that due to that hip injury?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was repeated after the -- during the war because there was shelling. And because of that shelling I had injuries but I also injured my hip again. I had injuries on my knee, below my knee, on my arm, my head.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you talked about this injury beforehand. Did that cause any problems for you or difficulties in serving in the fighting positions in May, June, and July 1998?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I did not spare myself because I had set myself a task to be a member of the KLA, and that's what I did. And I'm saying here frankly, I never thought I would come out of it alive but I wanted to become a part of the history for the defence of my people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yeah, I understand that and I believe you. My question is: Did this injury to your leg beforehand or your disability, does that have anything to do with why you were spending some of your time doing office work, keeping records?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if you remember, who was it that decided that you could do some office work and some fighting at the front lines or serving at the front lines?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was decided by Ymer Alushani, aka Voglushi.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did he decide it all by himself or did he discuss it with anyone else?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he decided it all by himself but he informed Qerqizi.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That's a good time for me, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you then, Mr. Nicholls. We will break for the evening. Do we take it you're near the end of your examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'll try to be brief tomorrow, Your Honour. I do have a little bit more to go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That is what is called a gentle hint. We will adjourn now until 2.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
